memory_update.text: Primary public-market federal-servicing candidates for this node are Nelnet (NNI) and Maximus (MMS/Aidvantage); MOHELA and EdFinancial appear important but are not straightforward US-listed common-equity candidates.

Private student-credit and refinance candidates include Sallie Mae (SLM), SoFi (SOFI), and Navient (NAVI/Earnest); these are direct but credit-cycle-sensitive rather than pure picks-and-shovels infrastructure suppliers.

The strongest chokepoint signal is not physical scarcity but regulated process capacity: few servicers, complex repayment-plan rules, borrower communications, delinquency/default processing, and compliance obligations.

Affordability analytics and education-verification/data infrastructure remain under-covered in the five-name limit; potential next-pass candidates include Equifax/The Work Number and private companies such as National Student Clearinghouse-linked vendors, Enterval, MARKETview, Sparrow, Tasseled, and PayForED.
Need current market-cap verification for NAVI before treating it as above the USD 1B preferred threshold; retain as direct-exposure candidate but label market-cap note as unknown until checked.

node: Student loans, repayment infrastructure, private refinancing, and affordability analytics
summary: Expanded universe around the student-financing chokepoint found a small set of US-listed companies with direct exposure to regulated student-loan servicing, private education lending, refinancing, and repayment infrastructure. The clearest scarce-supplier angle is federal loan servicing: Department of Education materials list only a small group of current servicers, with public-market exposure mainly through Nelnet and Maximus/Aidvantage. Private student-credit exposure maps to Sallie Mae, SoFi, and Navient/Earnest, but their economics depend on credit quality, funding costs, regulation, refinancing demand, and borrower stress rather than simply education enrollment growth.
